patterns: First versions: Dan Koe's 'the first version of anything will be embarrassing' is the biggest post of the day (~45k). Permission to be bad at the start keeps landing.
Fountain Pen Day is tomorrow (Nov 6). Pen posts are mostly newcomers, wrist comfort, messy fills, and 'what's your combo' prompts.
Handwriting as tech: an open-source engine of a million handwritten fonts that never repeats a letter got ~12k views on a ~1k account. Analog made strange by software is pulling attention.
Executive dysfunction confessions are everywhere, short and blunt, often about basic stuff like eating or laundry. Few replies, lots of recognition.
Morning pages are having a small comeback, with people posting that they started again.
Watchlist founder talk is Yongfook again, three posts past 5k, now on productized services over SaaS.

reply_ideas.description: a designer who released over a million free handwritten fonts from an open-source engine that never writes the same letter twice
reply_ideas.reply_text: I write by hand every day, and what I'd miss in a font is the way handwriting changes when you're tired or rushing. Does the engine change anything across a page, like letters getting looser toward the bottom, or is each letter different but just as steady?

reply_ideas.description: saying they still can't write honestly in their journal because their mom used to read it, and have taken year-long breaks because of it
reply_ideas.reply_text: I think the fear of someone reading it changes what you write even when nobody ever does. Have you tried writing the honest part on a loose sheet you can throw away after, or does it have to live in the journal to count?

reply_ideas.description: a small web and AI consultancy founder taking fountain pen notes during a talk about an AI voice notes app that talks back
reply_ideas.reply_text: Taking fountain pen notes at a talk about an app that talks back is my favorite kind of contradiction. Did anything he said make you want the app, or did the pen win?

bip_draft:

video_tip: 15 seconds, no face. Overhead on textured cream paper, a hand fills a fountain pen from a bottle, wipes the nib on a folded paper towel, then writes 'first version' at the top of the page. Pen and paper sounds only, no music. End on the wet ink. Post it tomorrow with the Fountain Pen Day post.

x_posts.title: Looks like laziness
x_posts.text:
My feed this morning was full of people saying executive dysfunction is wrecking their day, and one person said they couldn't even find the motivation to eat. I think it's so hard because from the outside it looks like laziness, so people end up blaming themselves on top of it.

What's the smallest thing that gets you moving on a day like that?
